settings.heading: In Her Purse
settings.intro: What she carries, and what she carries it in. Bags cut generous enough for a hardback, small leather things that keep the loose ends in order, and the odd object that earns its place at the bottom.
settings.note: Nothing here waits in a warehouse. Each piece is cut and finished after you claim it.

settings.intro: Everything currently in her purse, and the purse itself. Made to order, one at a time, over a few unhurried days.
settings.coming_heading: The rest is still being cut
settings.coming_text: The collection fills slowly, on purpose. A card case, a longer strap, the little pouch that keeps loose things from becoming a situation — each one gets its turn on the table.

settings.heading: The rule of the purse
settings.intro: Four opinions the house holds firmly, and will not be talked out of.
settings.footnote: Opinions subject to revision only by the other Betty.

settings.heading: It must hold a hardback
settings.text: A bag that cannot carry a book is a decoration. Ours are cut to take a hardback, a cardigan you'll regret not wearing, and whatever you picked up on the way home.

settings.heading: It should slouch
settings.text: Structure is for luggage. Suede that softens with handling, a shape that gives, and a strap across the front for the days it is genuinely full.

settings.heading: It arrives wearing something
settings.text: The house scarf comes knotted at the handle. Leave it there, wear it elsewhere, or keep it in the drawer with the good ribbon — we don't mind.

settings.heading: It is made after you ask
settings.text: Nothing sits in a warehouse getting creased. Yours is cut, finished, and signed off by the house once you claim it. Allow 3–5 days before it ships.

settings.body:
My grandmother's purse was an archive and a crime scene at once. A paperback with the spine long gone, a lipstick with no lid, three pens that did not work and one that did, a pressed flower from a wedding she had opinions about, and — always — something for me, produced at exactly the right moment.

I have never once wanted a tidy bag. I wanted a beautiful one, and large enough to be interesting.

settings.heading: The next one, by letter
settings.text: New pieces for the purse are announced first, by letter. No hype, no hurry — we write when there is something worth writing about.
settings.note: We write rarely and beautifully. Unsubscribe whenever, no hard feelings.
